title: BEA U.S. International Transactions and Investment Position, Q2 2026 — the market-valued companion to the TIC gross external debt print, same as-of quarter, six days earlier
source: EST: bea.gov/data/intl-trade-investment/international-investment-position, fetched direct 2026-09-16 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 54,660 bytes) by the tic-quarterly-external-debt-2026-09-30 D-14 adjacency sweep. The page's own release banner reads verbatim 'Current Release: June 24, 2026 | Next Release: September 24, 2026', with the current release titled 'U.S. International Transactions and Investment Position, 1st Quarter 2026 and Annual Update' — so the next edition is the 2nd Quarter 2026 one, as-of 2026-06-30. The same banner carries the current figures used as this proposal's anchor: net IIP -$21.27tn at end-Q1-2026, 'Assets totaled $43.37 trillion, and liabilities totaled $64.64 trillion', with end-Q4-2025 net at -$21.87tn (revised). Corroborated mechanically: 2026-09-24 is a Thursday, and BEA's quarterly IIP cadence of late-month-following-the-quarter reproduces the stated 2026-06-24 prior release for Q1. A SECOND independent primary was attempted and FAILED: bea.gov/news/schedule returned HTTP 200 (75,123 bytes) but its rendered text contains no 'International Investment Position' entry at all — the schedule table is not in the served HTML — so the release-schedule page was NOT read and is not cited here; the product page's own banner is the sole primary. Filed estimate on two counts, neither of them date doubt: a sweep-discovered proposal is always estimate by contract (docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md; scripts/event-scan-validation.mjs fails a non-estimate proposal), and the confirmed-tier BEA: prefix is reserved for the bea.gov release SCHEDULE, which is exactly the document that failed to serve. Checked 2026-09-16
notes: DISCOVERED by the tic-quarterly-external-debt-2026-09-30 D-14 pulse (2026-09-16), which found the U.S. IIP untracked in this calendar entirely — only japan-balance-of-payments-2026-12-08 and uk-balance-of-payments-2026-12-22 exist for any country. THE REASON TO TRACK IT, and it is specific rather than generic 'adjacent macro': this release publishes the SAME as-of 2026-06-30 reference quarter as tic-quarterly-external-debt-2026-09-30, SIX DAYS EARLIER, on the SAME subject — U.S. liabilities to foreigners. TIC gross external debt is the debt-instrument slice of the IIP's liabilities side: $30.197tn as-of 2026Q1 against the IIP's $64.64tn of total liabilities for the same quarter, a ratio of 0.467. That single ratio is ONE observation and is recorded as an anchor, not as an estimator — no forward test is registered on it and none should be until the ratio is measured across a real panel. THE MECHANICAL DIFFERENCE IS THE POINT AND IT IS PRIMARY-SOURCED: TIC Table A's own footnote 2/, verified unchanged on vintages spanning 2015Q1 to 2026Q1, reads 'All debts are presented at face value. Exception: long-term debt securities in the memorandum section are valued at market value, as recommended.' BEA's IIP is market-valued throughout. So the two measures of one quarter diverge by exactly the revaluation a rate move produces — which makes this release the natural control for reading the TIC print, and makes the pair jointly informative in a way neither is alone. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the same standing grounds the TIC ledger uses: a quarter-stale stock measure, no house playbook is macro-keyed, and nothing here licenses an entry. Proposed as an estimate.
